classification.difficultyReason: Uses decreasing rates and reverses the connected-rate calculation to find an edge rate.

content.prompt: A cubic block of ice is melting so that the block remains cubic.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If the edge is melting at $2\text{ cm/min}$, find the rate at which the volume is melting when the edge is $12\text{ cm}$.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the edge length in centimetres. Since it is decreasing, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-2\text{ cm/min}$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=x^3\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=\frac{dV}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=3x^2(-2)\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-6x^2.\end{aligned}$$
When $x=12$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{dt}&=-6(144)\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-864\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}.\end{aligned}$$
The volume decreases at $864\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the volume is melting at $75\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$, find the rate at which the edges are melting when the volume is $64\text{ cm}^3$.

answer.short: The edge length decreases at $\dfrac{25}{16}\text{ cm/min}$.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the edge length in centimetres. Here $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-75\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=x^3\\x^3&=64\\x&=4\text{ cm}\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=3x^2\frac{dx}{dt}\\-75&=3(16)\frac{dx}{dt}\\\frac{dx}{dt}&=-\frac{75}{48}\\\frac{dx}{dt}&=-\frac{25}{16}\text{ cm/min}.\end{aligned}$$
The edge length decreases at $\dfrac{25}{16}\text{ cm/min}$.
